questions.q: Why does the capstone track ROC AUC rather than relying on accuracy alone?
options: ROC AUC is always higher than accuracy
About a third of customers churn, so a model predicting 'nobody churns' already scores a decent accuracy
Accuracy cannot be computed for binary problems
ROC AUC works without a test set
questions.explain: With imbalanced classes, accuracy can look good for a useless model. ROC AUC measures how well the model ranks likely churners above loyal customers.

questions.q: What does stratify=y do in train_test_split?
options: Keeps the class proportions about the same in the train and test sets
Sorts the rows by the target
Removes rows with missing values
Scales the features
questions.explain: Stratification preserves the churn rate in both splits. Here it was 0.344 in training and 0.345 in test.

questions.q: The DummyClassifier(strategy='most_frequent') baseline scored accuracy 0.655 and ROC AUC 0.5. What does that tell you?
options: The dataset is corrupted
Any model that only reaches about 0.65 accuracy or 0.5 AUC has learned nothing useful
0.655 is an excellent accuracy
AUC cannot be computed for classifiers
questions.explain: The baseline predicts the majority class for everyone. A real model must clearly beat 0.5 AUC to justify its complexity.

questions.q: In the exploration, which group churned the most?
options: Two-year contract customers at 0.143
One-year contract customers at 0.254
Month-to-month customers at 0.462
All groups churned equally
questions.explain: Month-to-month customers churned at 0.462, versus 0.254 for one-year and 0.143 for two-year contracts.

questions.q: What is the rule for the test set during the capstone build?
options: Tune every model on it and keep the best score
Fit the scaler on the test set
Merge it back into training after each experiment
Keep it sealed: fit, impute, scale, and tune on training data only, and use the test set once at the end
questions.explain: Touching the test set during development leaks information and makes the final estimate optimistic.
